From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
ambulance
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

    Borrowed from French ambulance, which replaced hôpital ambulant (“moving hospital”) via the suffix -ance, from Latin ambulō (“to walk; to go about”).[1]

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈæm.bjə.ləns/, /ˈæm.bə.ləns/
    • (African-American Vernacular, also Southern US) IPA(key): /ˈæm.bjəˌlæns/, /ˈæm.bəˌlæns/
    • Audio (US):(file)
    • (Indic) IPA(key): /ˈamb(j)ʊləns/
    • Hyphenation: am‧bu‧lance

    Noun

    [edit]

    ambulance (plural ambulances)

    2. An emergency vehicle designed for transporting seriously ill or injured people to a hospital. [from 1854[1]]
      Synonyms: (slang) band-aid buggy, (slang) blood box, (slang) body box, (slang) bone box, (slang) meat wagon
      • 2025 December 12, Tobi Thomas, Denis Campbell, “NHS bracing for worst ever winter crisis in next fortnight amid rising flu cases”, in The Guardian‎[1]:
        The NHS is bracing itself for its worst ever winter crisis descending in the next fortnight because of a worsening “flu-nami” that has left hospitals, GP surgeries and ambulances services under intense strain.
    3. (military) A mobile field hospital. [from 1798[1]]
    4. (UK) A vehicle used for the transportation of dead people, typically to a mortuary.
      Synonym: private ambulance
    5. (chiefly UK, obsolete) Synonym of stretcher, a litter used for medical transport.
    6. (US, obsolete) Synonym of covered wagon. [from late 19th c.[1]]

    Verb

    [edit]

    ambulance (third-person singular simple present ambulances, present participle ambulancing, simple past and past participle ambulanced)

    1. (transitive) To transport by ambulance.
      • 1918, Western Surgical Association: Transactions, volume 27, page 66:
        Ambulancing patients with acute obstruction over cobble and rails should not be tolerated; better render the necessary service where the patient is found.

            Synonyms: ziekenauto, ziekenwagen
            • 1975, Anke de Vries, Het geheim van Mories Besjoer, Lemniscaat, →ISBN, →OCLC, section 59:
              Ze beschrijven uitvoerig hoe Maurice te hulp schoot, toen hij gegil hoorde, hoe hij iemand had zien wegvluchten uit de kamer en dat hij het was geweest, die een ambulance had gebeld.
              They described in detail how Maurice rushed to help when he heard screaming, how he had seen someone fleeing the room, and that it was he who had called an ambulance.
            • 1979, Rubberen Robbie, “De ambulance [The ambulance]”, in Zuipen (CD):
              Twee, drie, weken geleden kwam de ambulance ¶ Bij onze buurman hier net om de hoek
              Two, three weeks ago, the ambulance came ¶ To our neighbor's place just around the corner
